title: Powerboard/powerbars - decent quality ones
body:
What would you recommend for a 6-8 port good quality powerbar? All the cheap home stuff I have used (Click, HPM, ControlTec- basically Bunnings stuff) is… garbage. Sockets fail, which is not something I have ever experienced with overseas powerbars (admittedly my overseas gear was mostly UK plugs which are about five times as solid as AU plugs).
Belkin seems like the 'expensive' brand here, but overseas Belkin is positioned as pretty pedestrian and here it's somehow 'premium'. And on the 6/8 port boards all the sockets are jammed in really close which doesn't work with DC adaptors or AU plugs that are directional- i.e the design is a bit crap and I wouldn't be able to use all the ports anyway.
I'd be satisfied with rackmount style PDUs as long as I was getting something of decent value and not just paying higher prices for an 'industrial' form factor.
So:
* 6-8 ports
* Preferably decent spacing between ports
* I do not care about about surge protection
* Reliable internals so I never have to worry about bad connections (this is a huge problem with the budget brands)
Edit: Bunnings does sell more expensive boards, but… I don't trust Bunnings for quality electrical gear.
